method: Ranked by claude-sonnet-5-5, which read 11 of 14 shortlisted pieces

picks.title: My grandmother was a seal
picks.author: Jordan Lee Borgman
picks.why_it_matters: Irish families claimed selkie ancestry, and the essay reads that inheritance of theft and grief as a harder, more honest model of kinship with nature.

picks.title: A game you cannot win unless you have a quantum computer
picks.why_it_matters: A 3×3 parity puzzle with no classical solution becomes a quantum game won 98.3% of the time, showing contextuality as a resource and a hardware benchmark.

picks.title: The AI Forecasting Agenda
picks.author: Scott Alexander
picks.why_it_matters: Maps where AI forecasting still fails: conditional and causal questions, plus AI progress itself. Freeciv replays are proposed as a way to test causal forecasts.

picks.title: The Fall of China’s Last Emperor
picks.author: Paul French
picks.why_it_matters: Narrative history of Puyi and Wanrong's last years in the Forbidden City, drawing on unpublished letters that undercut the tutor Johnston's own memoir.

picks.title: The College Kids Who Drove a Duck Across the Americas
picks.author: April White
picks.why_it_matters: Nine college students drove a WWII amphibious truck across the Americas in 1961. Their letters show how a Cold War goodwill stunt actually went.
